item.title: Schools struggle to measure how much AI experiments are helping
item.description: Schools are experimenting with AI, and a lot of them are encountering the same problem: It's hard to measure whether the technology is good or bad for students.
item.content:encoded: Schools are experimenting with AI, and a lot of them are encountering the same problem: It's hard to measure whether the technology is good or bad for students.

item.title: Noah Adams, longtime host of NPR's 'All Things Considered,' has died
item.description: One of NPR's most gifted storytellers, Noah Adams' soft voice and vivid writing helped define the network's sound for a generation of Americans.

item.title: 'Lincoln in the Bardo' takes a distinctly American grief to the Met stage
item.description: With music by Missy Mazzoli, George Saunders' award-winning Civil War novel comes to surreal life in a stage adaptation making its world premiere at The Metropolitan Opera.

item.title: Disgruntled farmers may help flip Senate seat in Kansas
item.description: President Trump heads to Kansas to campaign for Republican candidates Monday but farmers disgruntled by White House policies may help flip a U.S. Senate seat that Republicans have held for almost a century.

item.title: 'Life is absolutely brutal in Gaza,' says World Food Programme head
item.description: The UN's World Food Programme says 1.4 million people in Gaza are suffering acute food shortages and that funding gaps are forcing cutbacks in critical aid, despite the U.S. brokered Hamas-Israel ceasefire.
